# What's open this week — and what to know before you go.

> ParkReady Guides by GOES Health · Week of Nov 9–15, 2026. Weekly entrance briefings for 6 of America's busiest national parks (17 open entrances): which entrances are open, this week's official closures and weather, and what to prepare for at that entrance and season. Every fact links to the National Park Service or National Weather Service page it came from.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/

Mid-November is shoulder season: many entrances and high roads are closed, services are thin, and weather turns fast. We only publish pages for entrances that are open; closures are listed on each park page.

## National parks this week

### [Yellowstone National Park](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/index.md)

WY · MT · ID · Winter shoulder season: only the North ↔ Northeast road is open to cars.

- [North Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/north-entrance.md): Open to cars (year-round road)
- [Northeast Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/northeast-entrance.md): Open to cars, reached via Gardiner
- Closed / limited: West Entrance (West Yellowstone, MT); South Entrance (from Grand Teton); East Entrance (from Cody, WY)

### [Yosemite National Park](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/index.md)

CA · Snow on the way: Tioga and Glacier Point roads close Nov 12 at 5 pm.

- [Arch Rock Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/arch-rock-entrance.md): Open — Hwy 140 / El Portal Road
- [Big Oak Flat Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/big-oak-flat-entrance.md): Open — weekday delays
- [South Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/south-entrance.md): Open — Winter Storm Watch
- [Hetch Hetchy Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/hetch-hetchy-entrance.md): Daylight only — closes for snow
- Closed / limited: Tioga Pass Entrance (Hwy 120 east, from Lee Vining); Glacier Point Road

### [Grand Canyon National Park](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/index.md)

AZ · Day use only on the South Rim: overnight lodging suspended, bring your own water.

- [South Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/south-entrance.md): Open 24/7 — day use, bring water
- [Desert View (East) Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/desert-view-east-entrance.md): Open 24/7
- [North Rim Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/north-rim-entrance.md): Limited day use — no services, closing soon
- Closed / limited: Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Black & Silver bridges, entire North Kaibab Trail

### [Great Smoky Mountains National Park](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/index.md)

TN · NC · Winter Weather Advisory on the Tennessee side; snow showers at Newfound Gap.

- [Gatlinburg Entrance (Sugarlands)](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/gatlinburg-entrance.md): Open — Winter Weather Advisory
- [Townsend Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/townsend-entrance.md): Open — Winter Weather Advisory
- [Cherokee Entrance (Oconaluftee)](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/cherokee-entrance.md): Open — elk area
- Closed / limited: Seasonal secondary roads

### [Zion National Park](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/index.md)

UT · Shuttle season ends Nov 28; cool days, cold canyon water, storms Friday night.

- [South Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/south-entrance.md): Open — shuttle through Nov 28
- [East Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/east-entrance.md): Open — gravel section, size limits
- [Kolob Canyons Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/kolob-canyons-entrance.md): Open — may close for snow or ice
- Closed / limited: Watchman Trail; Hidden Canyon / Observation Point from Zion Canyon

### [Glacier National Park](https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/index.md)

MT · Going-to-the-Sun Road closed at Avalanche Creek and Jackson Glacier Overlook for the season.

- [West Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/west-entrance.md): Open — road to Avalanche Creek
- [St. Mary Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/st-mary-entrance.md): Open — road to Jackson Glacier Overlook
- Closed / limited: Going-to-the-Sun Road alpine section (Logan Pass); Many Glacier and Two Medicine

## How ParkReady works

Each week we pull official alerts and operating hours from the NPS Data API, read each park's conditions, roads and news pages, and grab National Weather Service point forecasts for every entrance. We don't publish entrance wait times, wildlife sightings, or incident counts we can't source. If NPS hasn't said it, neither do we.

## Get the GOES app before the gate

**When signal drops, GOES steps in.** Many park entrances are the last reliable signal you'll have. Download GOES at the gate so its medical assessment, how-to guides and prevention tips work with zero bars.

# Yellowstone National Park this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · WY · MT · ID · Winter shoulder season: only the North ↔ Northeast road is open to cars. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/

Yellowstone closed its West, South and East entrances and nearly all roads to regular vehicles on Nov. 1. Until snowmobile and snowcoach season starts Dec. 15, the only way to drive into the park is the road between the North Entrance (Gardiner, MT) and the Northeast Entrance (Cooke City/Silver Gate, MT), through Mammoth Hot Springs, Tower Junction and Lamar Valley. Sources: [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm); [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm); [NPS Yellowstone alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

## Entrances open this week

- [North Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/north-entrance.md) (Gardiner, MT): **Open to cars (year-round road)**. The North Entrance at Gardiner, Montana is the only Yellowstone entrance open to wheeled vehicles all year, and right now it's one of only two ways to drive in. From here the road climbs to Mammoth Hot Springs and continues east through Tower Junction and Lamar Valley to the Northeast Entrance.
- [Northeast Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/northeast-entrance.md) (Cooke City & Silver Gate, MT): **Open to cars, reached via Gardiner**. The Northeast Entrance near Silver Gate and Cooke City, Montana sits at the far end of Yellowstone's only winter road. With the Beartooth Highway closed for the season, the way to Cooke City in winter is through the park from Gardiner and Lamar Valley.

## Closed or limited this week

- **West Entrance (West Yellowstone, MT).** Closed to cars Nov 1 – Dec 14 (shoulder season). Opens to commercially guided snowmobiles and snowcoaches Dec 15. Sources: [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **South Entrance (from Grand Teton).** Closed to cars Nov 1 – Dec 14. Opens to oversnow travel Dec 15. Sources: [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **East Entrance (from Cody, WY).** Closed to cars Nov 1 – Dec 14. Oversnow dates differ between NPS pages (Park Roads lists Dec 15; operating hours list Dec 22) — confirm before planning. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yellowstone fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## What matters in Yellowstone right now

- **Thermal areas (scald burns).** Burns from thermal features are a common cause of serious injury and death in Yellowstone. Ground that looks solid can be a thin crust over superheated water. Stay on boardwalks, keep kids close, and never touch runoff. More than 20 people have died after entering or falling into hot springs. Biscuit Basin (near Old Faithful) remains closed after the July 2024 hydrothermal explosion. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm); [NPS Yellowstone alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Bears.** All of Yellowstone is grizzly and black bear country. Stay at least 100 yards from bears and wolves, carry bear spray where you can reach it, hike in groups of 3+, make noise, and avoid carcasses. Since 1970, 91% of people injured by bears in Yellowstone were hiking alone or with one partner. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Bison, elk and other wildlife.** Stay at least 25 yards from bison, elk and all other animals (100 yards from bears, wolves and cougars). The safest view is usually from inside your car. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Winter driving and cold.** NPS asks fall and winter drivers to watch the weather, keep plans flexible, expect limited services and closures without notice, pack blankets and cold-weather essentials, and keep a full tank. Sources: [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Active Yellowstone NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Most Park Roads Closed to All Vehicles.** Most roads are closed to prepare for commercially-guided snowcoach and snowmobile travel during the winter season, which will begin December 15 (weather depending). The road between the North and Northeast entrances is the only road open year-round to regular vehicles. (https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **[Information] Traffic Delays - Gardner River High Bridge.** Expect a single lane of traffic with up to 15-minute delays, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from April 1 through November 24, 2026. Oversized/overweight vehicles (8'6"+ wide, 75'+ long, 80,000 lbs+ gross vehicle weight) will not be able to cross the bridge during this time. (https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **[Park Closure] Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion.** The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024. (https://www.nps.gov/yell/images/Biscuit_Basin_Closure_Map_20250529_1.png)

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Yellowstone North Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Yellowstone National Park · Gardiner, MT · Status: **Open to cars (year-round road)**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/north-entrance.html

The North Entrance at Gardiner, Montana is the only Yellowstone entrance open to wheeled vehicles all year, and right now it's one of only two ways to drive in. From here the road climbs to Mammoth Hot Springs and continues east through Tower Junction and Lamar Valley to the Northeast Entrance.

## This week at the North Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Open year-round to regular vehicles: North Entrance → Mammoth → Tower Junction → Lamar Valley → Northeast Entrance. Every other park road is closed to cars (oversnow travel only from Dec 15). Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm); [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Gardner River High Bridge (0.5 mi southeast of Mammoth, toward Tower): single-lane traffic with up to 15-minute delays, 24/7, through Nov 24, 2026. Vehicles 8'6"+ wide, 75'+ long or 80,000+ lbs can't cross. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm); [NPS Yellowstone alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Closed:** Mammoth to Norris is closed to cars; it opens to oversnow vehicles Dec 15, 2026. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **Open:** Open at Mammoth per NPS operating dates: Albright Visitor Center, Mammoth Campground (first-come, first-served after Oct 15), Mammoth General Store, Mammoth Medical Clinic (closed on Thanksgiving), Mammoth Hot Springs Hotel & Cabins, Post Office. The Mammoth gas station is listed as closed — fill up in Gardiner. Sources: [Yellowstone operating dates (updated Nov 9, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
- **Info:** Road status: call (307) 344-2117 or text 82190 to 888-777 for Yellowstone road alerts. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yellowstone fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Thermal terraces at Mammoth.** Mammoth Hot Springs is the main thermal area you can reach by car right now. Stay on boardwalks and designated trails; thermal runoff can burn. Pets aren't allowed on boardwalks or in thermal areas. If you feel sick in a thermal area, leave immediately — gases can build up. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Elk and bison around Mammoth and the road.** The rule: at least 25 yards from elk and bison, 100 yards from bears and wolves. If an animal moves toward you, back away. It's illegal to stay near any animal at a distance that disturbs it. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Bears may still be active.** NPS treats all of Yellowstone as bear country. Carry bear spray on any walk away from the car, hike in a group, and never leave packs or coolers unattended. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Cold, ice and short days.** This week's NWS forecast for Gardiner: highs around 55–64°F, lows in the mid-30s, with a chance of rain and snow showers by Saturday. NPS asks drivers to carry blankets and keep a full tank. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Checklist for the North Entrance

- [ ] **Fill the tank in Gardiner** — NPS lists the Mammoth gas station as closed for winter.
- [ ] **Download offline maps + the GOES app before the arch** — NPS says to dial 911 “if cell service is available” — don't plan around it.
- [ ] **Bear spray within reach** — One can per person, in a holster, not in the pack. NPS: spray when a charging bear is 30–60 ft away.
- [ ] **Pack winter layers and a blanket** — Even after a 60°F afternoon, nights drop near freezing.
- [ ] **Check road status the morning you go** — (307) 344-2117, or text 82190 to 888-777.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Yellowstone Northeast Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Yellowstone National Park · Cooke City & Silver Gate, MT · Status: **Open to cars, reached via Gardiner**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yellowstone/northeast-entrance.html

The Northeast Entrance near Silver Gate and Cooke City, Montana sits at the far end of Yellowstone's only winter road. With the Beartooth Highway closed for the season, the way to Cooke City in winter is through the park from Gardiner and Lamar Valley.

## This week at the Northeast Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Open year-round for wheeled vehicles between the North and Northeast entrances, through Lamar Valley. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Closed:** Beartooth Highway (US-212, Cooke City to Red Lodge): closed for the season. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Chief Joseph Scenic Byway (WY-296): in winter, 9 miles between Cooke City and Pilot Creek close to wheeled vehicles (oversnow only). That segment is normally open to cars mid-May through early November — check WYDOT before relying on it. Sources: [Yellowstone Park Roads (updated Nov 3, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **Closed:** Campgrounds near this entrance are closed: Slough Creek (seasonal) and Pebble Creek (closed until further notice for flood recovery). Tower-Roosevelt services are closed for the winter. Sources: [Yellowstone operating dates (updated Nov 9, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/hours.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yellowstone fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## Forecast near the Northeast Entrance

| Thursday | 65°F | Partly Sunny | 0 to 3 mph |
| Thursday Night | 28°F | Partly Cloudy | 2 mph |

| Friday Night | 28°F | Partly Cloudy | 3 mph |
| Saturday | 55°F | Partly Sunny then Chance Snow Showers | 1 to 5 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=45.004&lon=-110.005

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Lamar Valley wildlife: bison, wolves, bears.** Use pullouts, stay in or near your vehicle, keep 100 yards from wolves and bears and 25 yards from bison. Don't stop in the travel lane. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Bear country right up to town.** Hike in a group of 3+, make noise, carry bear spray, and if you find a carcass, leave by the way you came and report it. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Remote, cold and far from help.** This week's NWS forecast near Silver Gate: lows in the upper 20s, and a chance of snow showers Saturday. Services in the northeast corner are closed for the winter; the nearest year-round park facilities are back at Mammoth. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [Yellowstone operating dates (updated Nov 9, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Checklist for the Northeast Entrance

- [ ] **Plan an out-and-back trip** — With Beartooth closed, Cooke City is reached through the park from Gardiner.
- [ ] **Fuel, food and water for the whole drive** — Tower-Roosevelt services are closed.
- [ ] **Bear spray, traction and warm layers** — Lamar Valley pullouts get icy and cold at dawn and dusk.
- [ ] **Download GOES + offline maps in Gardiner** — Expect no signal on much of the route.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Yellowstone park-wide

- **Thermal areas (scald burns).** Burns from thermal features are a common cause of serious injury and death in Yellowstone. Ground that looks solid can be a thin crust over superheated water. Stay on boardwalks, keep kids close, and never touch runoff. More than 20 people have died after entering or falling into hot springs. Biscuit Basin (near Old Faithful) remains closed after the July 2024 hydrothermal explosion. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm); [NPS Yellowstone alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Bears.** All of Yellowstone is grizzly and black bear country. Stay at least 100 yards from bears and wolves, carry bear spray where you can reach it, hike in groups of 3+, make noise, and avoid carcasses. Since 1970, 91% of people injured by bears in Yellowstone were hiking alone or with one partner. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Bison, elk and other wildlife.** Stay at least 25 yards from bison, elk and all other animals (100 yards from bears, wolves and cougars). The safest view is usually from inside your car. Sources: [Yellowstone safety: thermal areas, wildlife, bears](https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Winter driving and cold.** NPS asks fall and winter drivers to watch the weather, keep plans flexible, expect limited services and closures without notice, pack blankets and cold-weather essentials, and keep a full tank. Sources: [News release: Most Yellowstone roads and entrances close Nov. 1, 2026 (Oct 21)](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/news/26026.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## All active Yellowstone NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Most Park Roads Closed to All Vehicles.** Most roads are closed to prepare for commercially-guided snowcoach and snowmobile travel during the winter season, which will begin December 15 (weather depending). The road between the North and Northeast entrances is the only road open year-round to regular vehicles. (https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **[Information] Traffic Delays - Gardner River High Bridge.** Expect a single lane of traffic with up to 15-minute delays, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from April 1 through November 24, 2026. Oversized/overweight vehicles (8'6"+ wide, 75'+ long, 80,000 lbs+ gross vehicle weight) will not be able to cross the bridge during this time. (https://www.nps.gov/yell/planyourvisit/parkroads.htm)
- **[Park Closure] Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion.** The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024. (https://www.nps.gov/yell/images/Biscuit_Basin_Closure_Map_20250529_1.png)

# Yosemite National Park this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · CA · Snow on the way: Tioga and Glacier Point roads close Nov 12 at 5 pm. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/

Yosemite is open 24 hours a day, but the high country is shutting down. NPS announced that Tioga Road (Hwy 120 through the park) and Glacier Point Road temporarily close Thursday, Nov 12 at 5 pm because snow is forecast. Wawona Road (Hwy 41), El Portal Road (Hwy 140) and Big Oak Flat Road (Hwy 120 west) are open. Carry tire chains: they can become mandatory at any time, even for 4WD. Sources: [NPS Yosemite alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

## Entrances open this week

- [Arch Rock Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/arch-rock-entrance.md) (El Portal / Mariposa (Hwy 140)): **Open — Hwy 140 / El Portal Road**. Arch Rock is the Highway 140 entrance from Merced, Mariposa and El Portal, along the Merced River. NPS puts it about 20–25 minutes from Yosemite Valley.
- [Big Oak Flat Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/big-oak-flat-entrance.md) (Groveland (Hwy 120 west)): **Open — weekday delays**. Big Oak Flat is the Highway 120 entrance from the Bay Area via Groveland, next to Hodgdon Meadow. With Tioga Road closing, Hwy 120 inside the park now leads only toward Crane Flat and Yosemite Valley (about 45 minutes away).
- [South Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/south-entrance.md) (Fish Camp / Oakhurst (Hwy 41)): **Open — Winter Storm Watch**. The South Entrance on Highway 41 from Fresno, Oakhurst and Fish Camp leads to the Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias, Wawona, and then Yosemite Valley, a little over an hour north.
- [Hetch Hetchy Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/hetch-hetchy-entrance.md) (Evergreen Road (off Hwy 120)): **Daylight only — closes for snow**. Hetch Hetchy is Yosemite's quiet northwest corner, a reservoir valley at about 3,900 feet reached on Evergreen and Hetch Hetchy roads off Hwy 120. NPS puts it about 1.5 hours from Yosemite Valley.

## Closed or limited this week

- **Tioga Pass Entrance (Hwy 120 east, from Lee Vining).** Tioga Road temporarily closes Thu Nov 12 at 5 pm for forecast snow, and no overnight parking is allowed on it. NPS says the Tioga Pass Entrance is closed from approximately November through late May or June, so there's no entrance page for it this week. Sources: [NPS Yosemite alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Glacier Point Road.** Temporarily closes Thu Nov 12 at 5 pm for forecast snow. Part of the Glacier Point Road area remains under a Dome Fire safety closure. Sources: [NPS Yosemite alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yosemite fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## What matters in Yosemite right now

- **Black bears in all areas.** NPS: bears remain active in all areas of the park. Store food properly, use bear-proof dumpsters, and stay at least 50 yards from bears in forest and meadows — but yell at and scare away a bear that approaches you or is in a developed area. Yosemite has an estimated 300–500 black bears and no grizzlies. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite bears](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/nature/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Rivers and slick rock.** Waterfalls are flowing low, as usual for November, but NPS still asks visitors to use caution along rivers and creeks: rocks are slippery even when dry. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Winter storm, chains and ice.** NWS Hanford issued a Winter Storm Watch (Nov 11, until Nov 17, 4 am PST) for the park's southern area, and the forecast calls for rain and thunderstorms Friday, with snow possible at higher elevations. Carry chains even with 4WD and expect icy spots on mostly dry roads. Sources: [NWS Hanford: Winter Storm Watch (issued Nov 11, until Nov 17 4 am PST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.507&lon=-119.632); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Smoke and air quality.** The Dome Fire (Sept–Oct) was 86% contained with minimal activity as of NPS's Oct 13 update, and fire closures remain around the Glacier Point Road area. Air quality can still be affected by fires elsewhere or prescribed burns, so check current AQI before strenuous hikes. Sources: [Dome Fire update, Oct 13, 2026](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/news/dome-fire-update-october-13-2026-morning.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [AirNow fire & smoke map](https://fire.airnow.gov/)
  - In GOES: Respiratory Hazards: smoke, pollution and pollen (AQI) monitoring

# Yosemite Arch Rock Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Yosemite National Park · El Portal / Mariposa (Hwy 140) · Status: **Open — Hwy 140 / El Portal Road**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

The Valley Loop Trail crossing at El Capitan Bridge is closed on weekdays. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

- **Info:** Fuel: 24/7 by credit card at El Portal, Wawona and Crane Flat. There's no gas in Yosemite Valley. Sources: [Yosemite driving directions, fuel & GPS warning](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/driving.htm)

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Merced River banks.** The river is low, but NPS warns rocks are slippery even when dry. Stay off wet granite near waterfalls and the river's edge. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Valley bears.** Bears are active in all areas, including the Valley. Use food lockers and bear-proof trash cans, and never leave food unattended at picnic spots. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite bears](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/nature/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Rain and thunderstorms Friday.** This week's NWS forecast for the Arch Rock area: sunny and about 66°F Thursday, then light rain and showers/thunderstorms Friday into Friday night. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

## Checklist for the Arch Rock Entrance

- [ ] **Fuel at El Portal or before** — No gas in the Valley.
- [ ] **Chains in the trunk** — Chains can become mandatory at any time, even with 4WD.
- [ ] **Follow road signs over GPS** — NPS: when your GPS and a road sign disagree, the sign is right.
- [ ] **Download GOES before the canyon** — Don't count on coverage in the Merced canyon and Valley.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Yosemite park-wide

- **Black bears in all areas.** NPS: bears remain active in all areas of the park. Store food properly, use bear-proof dumpsters, and stay at least 50 yards from bears in forest and meadows — but yell at and scare away a bear that approaches you or is in a developed area. Yosemite has an estimated 300–500 black bears and no grizzlies. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite bears](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/nature/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Rivers and slick rock.** Waterfalls are flowing low, as usual for November, but NPS still asks visitors to use caution along rivers and creeks: rocks are slippery even when dry. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Winter storm, chains and ice.** NWS Hanford issued a Winter Storm Watch (Nov 11, until Nov 17, 4 am PST) for the park's southern area, and the forecast calls for rain and thunderstorms Friday, with snow possible at higher elevations. Carry chains even with 4WD and expect icy spots on mostly dry roads. Sources: [NWS Hanford: Winter Storm Watch (issued Nov 11, until Nov 17 4 am PST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.507&lon=-119.632); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Smoke and air quality.** The Dome Fire (Sept–Oct) was 86% contained with minimal activity as of NPS's Oct 13 update, and fire closures remain around the Glacier Point Road area. Air quality can still be affected by fires elsewhere or prescribed burns, so check current AQI before strenuous hikes. Sources: [Dome Fire update, Oct 13, 2026](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/news/dome-fire-update-october-13-2026-morning.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [AirNow fire & smoke map](https://fire.airnow.gov/)
  - In GOES: Respiratory Hazards: smoke, pollution and pollen (AQI) monitoring

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

Call 209/372-0200 (then 1, 1) to check road conditions in the park.
- **[Information] No overnight parking on Tioga & Glacier Point Roads.** Overnight parking is not allowed on Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road, including all parking lots reachable from these roads.

# Yosemite Big Oak Flat Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Yosemite National Park · Groveland (Hwy 120 west) · Status: **Open — weekday delays**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/big-oak-flat-entrance.html

Big Oak Flat is the Highway 120 entrance from the Bay Area via Groveland, next to Hodgdon Meadow. With Tioga Road closing, Hwy 120 inside the park now leads only toward Crane Flat and Yosemite Valley (about 45 minutes away).

## This week at the Big Oak Flat Entrance (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** Big Oak Flat Road: open, with 15-minute delays on weekdays for fire-safety vegetation work between Foresta and Big Oak Flat. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Closed:** Tioga Road (east of Crane Flat) temporarily closes Thu Nov 12 at 5 pm for forecast snow. No overnight parking on Tioga Road. Sources: [NPS Yosemite alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Info:** Hodgdon Meadow Campground (by this entrance): open, first-come, first-served. Crane Flat, Tamarack Flat and White Wolf campgrounds are closed. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Info:** Fuel: Crane Flat, 24/7 by credit card. Sources: [Yosemite driving directions, fuel & GPS warning](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/driving.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yosemite fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

| Period | Temp | Forecast | Wind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tonight | 38°F | Clear | 10 mph |
| Thursday | 69°F | Sunny | 5 to 10 mph |
| Thursday Night | 35°F | Partly Cloudy then Chance Light Rain | 5 mph |

| Saturday | 50°F | Slight Chance Rain And Snow then Mostly Sunny | 0 to 5 mph |
| Saturday Night | 24°F | Mostly Cloudy | 0 to 5 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.8&lon=-119.874

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Freezing nights and wet snow.** This week's NWS forecast here: sunny and about 69°F Thursday, then rain and thunderstorms Friday, a Friday-night low near 27°F, and a chance of rain and snow. Being wet in freezing weather is how hikers get hypothermia. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Bears at campgrounds and pullouts.** Hodgdon Meadow is open. Use the food lockers, keep a clean camp, and stay 50 yards from bears in the forest. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite bears](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/nature/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Road work and wildlife on the road.** Expect weekday work zones on Big Oak Flat Road. NPS posts signs where bears have been hit by vehicles, so drive the speed limit. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite bears](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/nature/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals

## Checklist for the Big Oak Flat Entrance

- [ ] **Chains, even with 4WD** — Chains can become mandatory at any time.
- [ ] **Allow extra time on weekdays** — 15-minute delays on Big Oak Flat Road.
- [ ] **Don't plan on Tioga** — It closes Nov 12 at 5 pm.
- [ ] **Download GOES in Groveland** — Before the climb into the park.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Yosemite South Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Yosemite National Park · Fish Camp / Oakhurst (Hwy 41) · Status: **Open — Winter Storm Watch**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/south-entrance.html

The South Entrance on Highway 41 from Fresno, Oakhurst and Fish Camp leads to the Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias, Wawona, and then Yosemite Valley, a little over an hour north.

## This week at the South Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Wawona Road (Hwy 41): open. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Heads-up:** NWS Winter Storm Watch for this area, issued Nov 11, in effect until Nov 17 at 4 am PST. Sources: [NWS Hanford: Winter Storm Watch (issued Nov 11, until Nov 17 4 am PST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.507&lon=-119.632)
- **Info:** Mariposa Grove Road: open only to vehicles displaying a disability placard. Everyone else takes the free shuttle from the Mariposa Grove Welcome Plaza, which runs approximately late April through November. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Info:** Wawona Campground: open, reservation required until Nov 29. Bridalveil Creek Campground: closed. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Closed:** Glacier Point Road temporarily closes Thu Nov 12 at 5 pm. An area east of Wawona Road and south of Glacier Point Road remains closed after the Dome Fire; the Chilnualna Falls trail has reopened. Sources: [NPS Yosemite alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Info:** Fuel: Wawona, 24/7 by credit card. Sources: [Yosemite driving directions, fuel & GPS warning](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/driving.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yosemite fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## Forecast near the South Entrance

- **NWS Winter Storm Watch:** Winter Storm Watch issued November 11 at 5:33PM PST until November 17 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA

|---|---|---|---|

| Friday Night | 29°F | Showers And Thunderstorms then Slight Chance Rain And Snow | 0 to 10 mph |

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Winter storm on Hwy 41.** The NWS forecast here shows rain and thunderstorms Friday, then a chance of rain and snow with a low near 29°F. Chain controls can start with little notice. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [NWS Hanford: Winter Storm Watch (issued Nov 11, until Nov 17 4 am PST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.507&lon=-119.632); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Fire-scarred areas.** Stay out of the posted Dome Fire closure area. Burned slopes can drop rocks and trees, especially in rain. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Dome Fire update, Oct 13, 2026](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/news/dome-fire-update-october-13-2026-morning.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Bears in the groves and around Wawona.** Bears are active parkwide. Store food properly and keep your distance in forest and meadows. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals

- [ ] **Chains and a full tank** — Fuel at Wawona; carry chains even with 4WD.
- [ ] **Plan on the shuttle for Mariposa Grove** — Private cars need a disability placard.
- [ ] **Download GOES in Oakhurst or Fish Camp** — Before you drive into the forest.

Air quality can still be affected by fires elsewhere or prescribed burns, so check current AQI before strenuous hikes. Sources: [Dome Fire update, Oct 13, 2026](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/news/dome-fire-update-october-13-2026-morning.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [AirNow fire & smoke map](https://fire.airnow.gov/)
  - In GOES: Respiratory Hazards: smoke, pollution and pollen (AQI) monitoring

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road will temporarily close on Nov. 12 at 5 pm.** Tioga Road (continuation of Highway 120 through the park) and Glacier Point Road will temporarily close on Thursday, November 12, at 5 pm due to a forecast of snow. Call 209/372-0200 (then 1, 1) to check road conditions in the park.
- **[Information] No overnight parking on Tioga & Glacier Point Roads.** Overnight parking is not allowed on Tioga Road and Glacier Point Road, including all parking lots reachable from these roads.

# Yosemite Hetch Hetchy Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Yosemite National Park · Evergreen Road (off Hwy 120) · Status: **Daylight only — closes for snow**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/yosemite/hetch-hetchy-entrance.html

Hetch Hetchy is Yosemite's quiet northwest corner, a reservoir valley at about 3,900 feet reached on Evergreen and Hetch Hetchy roads off Hwy 120. NPS puts it about 1.5 hours from Yosemite Valley.

## This week at the Hetch Hetchy Entrance (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** Hetch Hetchy Road: open sunrise to sunset only, and closed when it's snowing or snow is forecast overnight. Day visitors must leave by sunset; the road is closed to all vehicles overnight. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite operating hours (Hetch Hetchy daylight hours)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Open:** No current trail closures in the Hetch Hetchy area. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Info:** Swimming and boating are prohibited in the reservoir (it's a drinking water supply). Pets aren't allowed on the dam or trails. Sources: [Yosemite: Hetch Hetchy day hikes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/hetchhetchy.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Yosemite fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## Forecast near the Hetch Hetchy Entrance

| Period | Temp | Forecast | Wind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tonight | 40°F | Clear | 5 to 10 mph |
| Thursday | 73°F | Sunny | 5 to 10 mph |
| Thursday Night | 36°F | Partly Cloudy then Slight Chance Light Rain | 5 mph |
| Friday | 56°F | Rain then Showers And Thunderstorms | 5 to 15 mph |

| Saturday Night | 26°F | Partly Cloudy | 0 to 10 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.886&lon=-119.841

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Getting caught by darkness.** Sunset comes early in mid-November and the gate closes at sunset. Turn around with daylight to spare: a twisted ankle on the Wapama Falls trail can turn into a cold night out. Sources: [Yosemite operating hours (Hetch Hetchy daylight hours)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [Yosemite: Hetch Hetchy day hikes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/hetchhetchy.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Rattlesnakes and poison oak.** NPS's Hetch Hetchy page tells hikers to watch for rattlesnakes and poison oak. Sources: [Yosemite: Hetch Hetchy day hikes](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/hetchhetchy.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters (venomous snakes) + Poisonous Plants (poison oak, ivy, sumac)
- **Storm closures.** Friday's NWS forecast here has rain and thunderstorms with a low near 28°F that night. If snow is forecast overnight, the road may not open. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Checklist for the Hetch Hetchy Entrance

- [ ] **Call before you drive** — 209/372-0200, then press 1, 1 for current road conditions.
- [ ] **Be out before sunset** — The road is gated overnight.
- [ ] **Water, sunscreen and a map** — NPS's own Hetch Hetchy checklist.
- [ ] **Download GOES before the turnoff** — Snakebite and poisonous-plant guidance that works offline.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Yosemite park-wide

- **Black bears in all areas.** NPS: bears remain active in all areas of the park. Store food properly, use bear-proof dumpsters, and stay at least 50 yards from bears in forest and meadows — but yell at and scare away a bear that approaches you or is in a developed area. Yosemite has an estimated 300–500 black bears and no grizzlies. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Yosemite bears](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/nature/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Rivers and slick rock.** Waterfalls are flowing low, as usual for November, but NPS still asks visitors to use caution along rivers and creeks: rocks are slippery even when dry. Sources: [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Winter storm, chains and ice.** NWS Hanford issued a Winter Storm Watch (Nov 11, until Nov 17, 4 am PST) for the park's southern area, and the forecast calls for rain and thunderstorms Friday, with snow possible at higher elevations. Carry chains even with 4WD and expect icy spots on mostly dry roads. Sources: [NWS Hanford: Winter Storm Watch (issued Nov 11, until Nov 17 4 am PST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.507&lon=-119.632); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Smoke and air quality.** The Dome Fire (Sept–Oct) was 86% contained with minimal activity as of NPS's Oct 13 update, and fire closures remain around the Glacier Point Road area. Air quality can still be affected by fires elsewhere or prescribed burns, so check current AQI before strenuous hikes. Sources: [Dome Fire update, Oct 13, 2026](https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/news/dome-fire-update-october-13-2026-morning.htm); [Yosemite Current Conditions (updated Nov 11, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [AirNow fire & smoke map](https://fire.airnow.gov/)
  - In GOES: Respiratory Hazards: smoke, pollution and pollen (AQI) monitoring

Call 209/372-0200 (then 1, 1) to check road conditions in the park.

# Grand Canyon National Park this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · AZ · Day use only on the South Rim: overnight lodging suspended, bring your own water. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/

This is not a normal November at Grand Canyon. An Aug. 29 flash flood badly damaged the Transcanyon Waterline. The South Rim is under Stage 4 water restrictions, overnight accommodations are suspended (dry camping only), and visitors are asked to bring their own water. The park is open for day use, and food service, the Grand Canyon Clinic and the Post Office remain open. In September NPS projected that pumping could restart around Nov. 16, with phased overnight service around Thanksgiving; it called those dates tentative. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [News release: Projected dates for restoring water to the South Rim (Sep 19, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/grand-canyon-national-park-announces-projected-dates-for-restoring-water-to-south-rim.htm); [News release: Stage 2 fire restrictions rescinded on South Rim (Nov 4, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/stage-2-fire-restrictions-rescinded-on-south-rim.htm)

## Entrances open this week

- [South Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/south-entrance.md) (Tusayan, AZ (Hwy 64 / 180)): **Open 24/7 — day use, bring water**. The South Entrance just north of Tusayan is the main gate into Grand Canyon's South Rim (NPS says it gets the most traffic). It leads to Grand Canyon Village, the main visitor center and the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trailheads.
- [Desert View (East) Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/desert-view-east-entrance.md) (Cameron, AZ (SR 64 via US 89)): **Open 24/7**. The East Entrance at Desert View is 25 miles west of Cameron on State Route 64, reached via US 89 through the Navajo Nation. It's 32 miles east of Grand Canyon Village, and NPS says waits here are usually shorter than at the South Entrance.
- [North Rim Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/north-rim-entrance.md) (Jacob Lake, AZ (SR 67)): **Limited day use — no services, closing soon**. The North Rim entrance station is on State Route 67, 30 miles south of Jacob Lake. In fall 2026 the North Rim is in modified operations: day use only, with no services. The gate closes for winter at sunset Nov 30 or after the first major snowstorm, whichever comes first.

## Closed or limited this week

- **Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Black & Silver bridges, entire North Kaibab Trail.** Closed after flash flooding, with no estimated reopening. Boat Beach is closed except for emergencies and brief scouting. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm); [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (cash is not accepted at the entrances). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## What matters in Grand Canyon right now

- **Water: bring your own.** Stage 4 restrictions are in effect on the South Rim. Inner-canyon water is off everywhere (1.5 Mile and 3 Mile resthouses, Havasupai Gardens) for the rest of the winter. Potable water tanks are at the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trailheads. Carry all your water or a reliable treatment method. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm); [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Elevation.** The South Rim is about 7,000 ft and the North Rim about 8,000 ft. NPS warns the altitude and dry air can cause dehydration, nausea, shortness of breath and exhaustion, so take your time at overlooks. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: High Altitude Illness: personalized altitude risk
- **The rim edge and ice.** Stay on trails and walkways, at least 6 feet from the edge, and never climb railings. In winter, walkways can be icy; NPS recommends over-the-shoe traction and hiking poles. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Inner canyon hiking.** Temperatures rise about 5.5°F for every 1,000 ft you descend. Rescue isn't guaranteed and response can be delayed. Rockfall is common during or after rain and freeze/thaw, and flash floods can hit with no warning. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Active Grand Canyon NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] INNER CANYON TRAIL CLOSURES.** Current trail closures: the entire North Kaibab Trail (including Cottonwood Campground), Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Silver Bridge, and the Black Bridge. Please do not attempt to access the closed areas.
- **[Caution] Overnight Lodging Suspended and Parkwide Stage 4 Water Restrictions.** Grand Canyon National Park has implemented Stage 4 water restrictions on the South Rim due to extensive flash flood damage to the Transcanyon Waterline. Overnight accommodations are suspended, and only dry camping is allowed. The park remains open for day use, with food and beverage services, the Grand Canyon Clinic, and Post Office remaining open. Visitors are asked to bring water with them when visiting the park. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/grand-canyon-national-park-to-close-overnight-hotel-accommodations-beginning-august-31.htm)
- **[Danger] INNER CANYON WATER SHUTOFFS.** Beginning Sep. 6, no potable water will be available in the inner canyon, including along the Bright Angel Trail (1.5 Mile Resthouse, 3-Mile Resthouse, Havasupai Gardens day use and campground). All backpackers and hikers should carry water filtration and treatment OR carry all water with them. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)
- **[Caution] Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures.** Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Grand Canyon South Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Grand Canyon National Park · Tusayan, AZ (Hwy 64 / 180) · Status: **Open 24/7 — day use, bring water**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/south-entrance.html

The South Entrance just north of Tusayan is the main gate into Grand Canyon's South Rim (NPS says it gets the most traffic). It leads to Grand Canyon Village, the main visitor center and the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trailheads.

## This week at the South Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Credit cards and America the Beautiful passes accepted; cash is not accepted. Sources: [Grand Canyon operating hours](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Heads-up:** NPS notes this station has the longest lines, with waits of up to 2 hours between 9:30 am and 4 pm. That's NPS's general guidance, not a live wait time. Desert View (East) usually has shorter waits. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Overnight accommodations are suspended; only dry camping is allowed. Food and beverage services, the Grand Canyon Clinic and the Post Office remain open. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [News release linked from the NPS alert: overnight accommodations suspended](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/grand-canyon-national-park-to-close-overnight-hotel-accommodations-beginning-august-31.htm)
- **Info:** Stage 2 fire restrictions were lifted on the South Rim Nov 4; Stage 1 remains. Campfires at Mather Campground are allowed only in established rings. Sources: [News release: Stage 2 fire restrictions rescinded on South Rim (Nov 4, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/stage-2-fire-restrictions-rescinded-on-south-rim.htm)
- **Open:** Open trails: Bright Angel to River Resthouse, Plateau Point, River Trail, South Kaibab to the Black Bridge, and Tonto Trail (Tip-Off to Havasupai Gardens). Expect intermittent closures for Bright Angel Trail repairs. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (cash is not accepted at the entrances). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## Forecast near the South Entrance

| Period | Temp | Forecast | Wind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tonight | 28°F | Clear | 7 mph |
| Thursday | 60°F | Sunny | 5 to 8 mph |
| Thursday Night | 30°F | Partly Cloudy | 6 mph |
| Friday | 57°F | Partly Sunny then Slight Chance Rain Showers | 3 to 8 mph |
| Friday Night | 36°F | Showers And Thunderstorms | 5 to 8 mph |
| Saturday | 48°F | Showers And Thunderstorms | 2 to 10 mph |
| Saturday Night | 26°F | Mostly Clear | 2 mph |
| Sunday | 50°F | Mostly Sunny | 1 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=35.993&lon=-112.121

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Dehydration in high, dry air.** At 7,000 feet in desert air you lose water fast, and the park is asking everyone to bring their own. Inner-canyon water stations are off. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm); [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)
  - In GOES: High Altitude Illness: personalized altitude risk
- **Cold mornings and icy rim paths.** NWS forecast for the South Rim this week: lows near 28–30°F, highs around 57–60°F, and showers and thunderstorms Friday night into Saturday. Freeze/thaw increases rockfall on trails. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Hiking down is the easy half.** NPS: rescue is not guaranteed and response can be delayed. If you feel nauseated, dizzy or exhausted, stop, rest, and slowly eat and drink. Don't force fluids; drinking too much can cause hyponatremia. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides

## Checklist for the South Entrance

- [ ] **Water for everyone, plus treatment if hiking** — Stage 4 restrictions; inner-canyon water is off.
- [ ] **Book a bed outside the park** — Overnight lodging in the park is suspended.
- [ ] **Card, not cash, at the gate** — Cash isn't accepted.
- [ ] **Traction devices for icy walkways** — NPS recommends them in winter.
- [ ] **Download GOES in Tusayan** — Before you're on the rim or below it.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Grand Canyon park-wide

- **Water: bring your own.** Stage 4 restrictions are in effect on the South Rim. Inner-canyon water is off everywhere (1.5 Mile and 3 Mile resthouses, Havasupai Gardens) for the rest of the winter. Potable water tanks are at the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trailheads. Carry all your water or a reliable treatment method. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm); [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Elevation.** The South Rim is about 7,000 ft and the North Rim about 8,000 ft. NPS warns the altitude and dry air can cause dehydration, nausea, shortness of breath and exhaustion, so take your time at overlooks. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: High Altitude Illness: personalized altitude risk
- **The rim edge and ice.** Stay on trails and walkways, at least 6 feet from the edge, and never climb railings. In winter, walkways can be icy; NPS recommends over-the-shoe traction and hiking poles. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Inner canyon hiking.** Temperatures rise about 5.5°F for every 1,000 ft you descend. Rescue isn't guaranteed and response can be delayed. Rockfall is common during or after rain and freeze/thaw, and flash floods can hit with no warning. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## All active Grand Canyon NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] INNER CANYON TRAIL CLOSURES.** Current trail closures: the entire North Kaibab Trail (including Cottonwood Campground), Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Silver Bridge, and the Black Bridge. Please do not attempt to access the closed areas.
- **[Caution] Overnight Lodging Suspended and Parkwide Stage 4 Water Restrictions.** Grand Canyon National Park has implemented Stage 4 water restrictions on the South Rim due to extensive flash flood damage to the Transcanyon Waterline. Overnight accommodations are suspended, and only dry camping is allowed. The park remains open for day use, with food and beverage services, the Grand Canyon Clinic, and Post Office remaining open. Visitors are asked to bring water with them when visiting the park. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/grand-canyon-national-park-to-close-overnight-hotel-accommodations-beginning-august-31.htm)
- **[Danger] INNER CANYON WATER SHUTOFFS.** Beginning Sep. 6, no potable water will be available in the inner canyon, including along the Bright Angel Trail (1.5 Mile Resthouse, 3-Mile Resthouse, Havasupai Gardens day use and campground). All backpackers and hikers should carry water filtration and treatment OR carry all water with them. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)
- **[Caution] Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures.** Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)

# Grand Canyon Desert View (East) Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Grand Canyon National Park · Cameron, AZ (SR 64 via US 89) · Status: **Open 24/7**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/desert-view-east-entrance.html

The East Entrance at Desert View is 25 miles west of Cameron on State Route 64, reached via US 89 through the Navajo Nation. It's 32 miles east of Grand Canyon Village, and NPS says waits here are usually shorter than at the South Entrance.

## This week at the Desert View (East) Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Credit cards and passes accepted; cash is not accepted. Sources: [Grand Canyon operating hours](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Info:** NPS says most Desert View services are open. Desert View Campground is seasonal (NPS lists an April–October season). Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Park-wide: Stage 4 water restrictions and suspended overnight accommodations. Bring your own water. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (cash is not accepted at the entrances). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

# Grand Canyon North Rim Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Grand Canyon National Park · Jacob Lake, AZ (SR 67) · Status: **Limited day use — no services, closing soon**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/grand-canyon/north-rim-entrance.html

The North Rim entrance station is on State Route 67, 30 miles south of Jacob Lake. In fall 2026 the North Rim is in modified operations: day use only, with no services. The gate closes for winter at sunset Nov 30 or after the first major snowstorm, whichever comes first.

## This week at the North Rim Entrance (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** North Rim: limited fall day use only. NO SERVICES — the campground, store and gas station are closed, and there's no fuel inside the park. Sources: [Grand Canyon Alerts & Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [News release: Modified fall operations at the North Rim (Sep 30, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/modified-fall-operations-north-rim-2026.htm)
- **Heads-up:** The SR 67 entrance gate closes at sunset Nov 30, 2026, or after the first major snowstorm, whichever comes first. NWS forecasts snow showers here Friday night and Saturday, so check before you drive. Sources: [News release: Modified fall operations at the North Rim (Sep 30, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/modified-fall-operations-north-rim-2026.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
- **Closed:** All North Rim water is off. The North Kaibab Trail is closed in its entirety. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)
- **Info:** Stage 2 fire restrictions remain in effect on the North Rim for the rest of 2026. Sources: [News release: Stage 2 fire restrictions rescinded on South Rim (Nov 4, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/stage-2-fire-restrictions-rescinded-on-south-rim.htm)
- **Info:** Road conditions: Arizona Highway Information, 1-888-411-ROAD (7623). Nearest lodging, food and fuel: Jacob Lake, about 45 miles north. Sources: [News release: Modified fall operations at the North Rim (Sep 30, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/modified-fall-operations-north-rim-2026.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (cash is not accepted at the entrances). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Grand Canyon fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
