## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Snow at 8,000 feet.** NPS: snow, ice and rain are common here this time of year. NWS forecast this week: highs around 47–52°F, lows near 28°F, and snow showers likely Friday night into Saturday with gusts over 20 mph. Sources: [News release: Modified fall operations at the North Rim (Sep 30, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/modified-fall-operations-north-rim-2026.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Very limited emergency response.** NPS says emergency response on the North Rim will be extremely limited and response times may be significantly delayed. Travel self-sufficient. Sources: [News release: Modified fall operations at the North Rim (Sep 30, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/modified-fall-operations-north-rim-2026.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Altitude.** The North Rim is about 8,000 ft. Take it slow if you've come up from lower elevations. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: High Altitude Illness: personalized altitude risk

## Checklist for the North Rim Entrance

- [ ] **Full tank at Jacob Lake or before** — No fuel in the park.
- [ ] **All the food, water and warm gear you need** — No services at all on the North Rim.
- [ ] **Check that the gate is still open** — 1-888-411-ROAD. The first big snowstorm can close it before Nov 30.
- [ ] **Download GOES before Jacob Lake** — You'll be far from help and likely out of signal.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Grand Canyon park-wide

- **Water: bring your own.** Stage 4 restrictions are in effect on the South Rim. Inner-canyon water is off everywhere (1.5 Mile and 3 Mile resthouses, Havasupai Gardens) for the rest of the winter. Potable water tanks are at the Bright Angel and South Kaibab trailheads. Carry all your water or a reliable treatment method. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm); [NPS Grand Canyon alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Elevation.** The South Rim is about 7,000 ft and the North Rim about 8,000 ft. NPS warns the altitude and dry air can cause dehydration, nausea, shortness of breath and exhaustion, so take your time at overlooks. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: High Altitude Illness: personalized altitude risk
- **The rim edge and ice.** Stay on trails and walkways, at least 6 feet from the edge, and never climb railings. In winter, walkways can be icy; NPS recommends over-the-shoe traction and hiking poles. Sources: [Grand Canyon safety: elevation, rim edges, winter](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Inner canyon hiking.** Temperatures rise about 5.5°F for every 1,000 ft you descend. Rescue isn't guaranteed and response can be delayed. Rockfall is common during or after rain and freeze/thaw, and flash floods can hit with no warning. Sources: [Grand Canyon Key Hiking Messages (updated Oct 27, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm); [News release: Select inner canyon trails reopen (Oct 26, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/select-inner-canyon-trails-reopen-in-grand-canyon-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## All active Grand Canyon NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] INNER CANYON TRAIL CLOSURES.** Current trail closures: the entire North Kaibab Trail (including Cottonwood Campground), Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Silver Bridge, and the Black Bridge. Please do not attempt to access the closed areas.
- **[Caution] Overnight Lodging Suspended and Parkwide Stage 4 Water Restrictions.** Grand Canyon National Park has implemented Stage 4 water restrictions on the South Rim due to extensive flash flood damage to the Transcanyon Waterline. Overnight accommodations are suspended, and only dry camping is allowed. The park remains open for day use, with food and beverage services, the Grand Canyon Clinic, and Post Office remaining open. Visitors are asked to bring water with them when visiting the park. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/learn/news/grand-canyon-national-park-to-close-overnight-hotel-accommodations-beginning-august-31.htm)
- **[Danger] INNER CANYON WATER SHUTOFFS.** Beginning Sep. 6, no potable water will be available in the inner canyon, including along the Bright Angel Trail (1.5 Mile Resthouse, 3-Mile Resthouse, Havasupai Gardens day use and campground). All backpackers and hikers should carry water filtration and treatment OR carry all water with them. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)
- **[Caution] Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures.** Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability. (https://www.nps.gov/grca/planyourvisit/key-messages.htm)

# Great Smoky Mountains National Park this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · TN · NC · Winter Weather Advisory on the Tennessee side; snow showers at Newfound Gap. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/

The Smokies' primary roads (Newfound Gap Road/US-441, Little River Road and Laurel Creek Road) are open 24/7 year-round, weather permitting. This week NWS Morristown has a Winter Weather Advisory for the Gatlinburg and Townsend areas until 7 am EST Nov 14, and the forecast at Newfound Gap shows snow showers Friday. There's no entrance fee, but any vehicle parked longer than 15 minutes needs a parking tag ($5 daily, $15 weekly, $40 annual). Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [NWS Morristown: Winter Weather Advisory (issued Nov 11, until Nov 14 7 am EST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=35.685&lon=-83.537); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)

## Entrances open this week

- [Gatlinburg Entrance (Sugarlands)](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/gatlinburg-entrance.md) (Gatlinburg, TN (US-441)): **Open — Winter Weather Advisory**. The Gatlinburg entrance on US-441 leads to Sugarlands Visitor Center and then up Newfound Gap Road over the crest to North Carolina. It's one of the park's three main entrances.
- [Townsend Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/townsend-entrance.md) (Townsend, TN (TN-73)): **Open — Winter Weather Advisory**. The Townsend entrance on TN-73 is the 'quiet side' gateway to Little River Road, Laurel Creek Road and Cades Cove.
- [Cherokee Entrance (Oconaluftee)](https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/cherokee-entrance.md) (Cherokee, NC (US-441)): **Open — elk area**. The Cherokee entrance on US-441 in North Carolina leads to Oconaluftee Visitor Center and the Mountain Farm Museum, then north up Newfound Gap Road to the state line.

## Closed or limited this week

- **Seasonal secondary roads.** Heintooga Ridge Road, Parson Branch Road and Rich Mountain Road are closed for the season. Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road are closed. Park Headquarters Road is closed for water and wastewater work. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)

**Entrance fee:** No entrance fee. A parking tag is required for any vehicle parked more than 15 minutes: daily $5, weekly $15, annual $40. America the Beautiful passes are not accepted in place of a tag. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [NPS Great Smoky Mountains fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

## What matters in Great Smoky Mountains right now

- **Black bears.** Over the last 10 years the Smokies averaged 339 reported negative human–bear encounters a year. In fall, bears feed heavily (up to 20,000 calories a day) and show up near roadsides. Approaching within 50 yards (150 ft) is illegal. If a black bear attacks and isn't after your food, fight back; don't play dead. Sources: [Smokies black bears](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/nature/black-bears.htm); [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Elk.** It's illegal to approach elk within 25 yards (75 ft). During the fall rut, bulls can be aggressive toward people, vehicles and pets. NPS closed the fields around Oconaluftee and Cataloochee to visitors during the rut, so obey any posted closures. Sources: [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm); [News release: Approaching elk is dangerous and illegal (Oct 7, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-approaching-elk-is-both-dangerous-and-illegal.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Wet cold and fast-changing mountain weather.** Temperatures can vary 10–20°F between base and summit, and clear skies lower down don't guarantee the same up high. Rain, then snow, then near-freezing nights is a textbook setup for hypothermia. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **GPS and no signal.** NPS warns that GPS units may send drivers the wrong way on one-way roads or to dead ends, and points mobile users to offline maps for areas without cell service. Sources: [Smokies directions & GPS warning](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/directions.htm)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

## Active Great Smoky Mountains NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Seasonal road closures.** Heintooga Ridge Road, Parson Branch Road, and Rich Mountain Road are closed for the season. (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **[Park Closure] Park Headquarters Road is closed.** Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.
- **[Park Closure] Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road closed..** Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road (Heintooga Round-Bottom Road) are closed. (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **[Information] Most visitors need a parking tag.** All vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes require a parking tag. Three tag durations are available for purchase for all vehicle sizes and types: Daily ($5), Weekly ($15), or Annual ($40). (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Great Smoky Mountains Gatlinburg Entrance (Sugarlands): this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Great Smoky Mountains National Park · Gatlinburg, TN (US-441) · Status: **Open — Winter Weather Advisory**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/gatlinburg-entrance.html

The Gatlinburg entrance on US-441 leads to Sugarlands Visitor Center and then up Newfound Gap Road over the crest to North Carolina. It's one of the park's three main entrances.

## This week at the Gatlinburg Entrance (Sugarlands) (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** Newfound Gap Road (US-441) is a primary road, open 24/7 year-round, weather permitting. NWS forecasts snow showers at Newfound Gap Friday, and snow and ice can close the road. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)

- **Open:** Roaring Fork Motor Nature Trail: open through Nov 29 (one-way and steep; no RVs, buses or vans over 25 ft, and no trailers). Kuwohi Road (formerly Clingmans Dome Road): open through Nov 29, subject to closures for snow and ice. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [Smokies current conditions & trail closures](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

America the Beautiful passes are not accepted in place of a tag. ## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Icy curves on US-441.** The NWS forecast at Newfound Gap has snow showers Friday (high near 32°F, low near 24°F Friday night). The climb from Sugarlands can go from wet to icy quickly, so check road status before crossing the crest. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Roadside bears.** Fall is peak feeding time. Use pull-offs, get fully off the road, and stay 50 yards away. Never feed bears, and put trash in bear-proof containers. Sources: [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm); [Smokies black bears](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/nature/black-bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Hypothermia on a 'mild' day.** This week in Gatlinburg: rain showers and about 53°F Thursday, then rain and snow showers Friday. Wet cotton plus wind is how hypothermia happens in mild weather. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Checklist for the Gatlinburg Entrance (Sugarlands)

- [ ] **Buy a parking tag first** — Required for any stop over 15 minutes; most trailheads have no tag machine.
- [ ] **Check US-441 before crossing into NC** — Snow showers are forecast at the crest this week.
- [ ] **Rain shell and warm, non-cotton layers** — Summit temps run 10–20°F colder than town.
- [ ] **Download GOES in Gatlinburg** — Before the signal drops on the climb.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Great Smoky Mountains park-wide

- **Black bears.** Over the last 10 years the Smokies averaged 339 reported negative human–bear encounters a year. In fall, bears feed heavily (up to 20,000 calories a day) and show up near roadsides. Approaching within 50 yards (150 ft) is illegal. If a black bear attacks and isn't after your food, fight back; don't play dead. Sources: [Smokies black bears](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/nature/black-bears.htm); [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Elk.** It's illegal to approach elk within 25 yards (75 ft). During the fall rut, bulls can be aggressive toward people, vehicles and pets. NPS closed the fields around Oconaluftee and Cataloochee to visitors during the rut, so obey any posted closures. Sources: [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm); [News release: Approaching elk is dangerous and illegal (Oct 7, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-approaching-elk-is-both-dangerous-and-illegal.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Wet cold and fast-changing mountain weather.** Temperatures can vary 10–20°F between base and summit, and clear skies lower down don't guarantee the same up high. Rain, then snow, then near-freezing nights is a textbook setup for hypothermia. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **GPS and no signal.** NPS warns that GPS units may send drivers the wrong way on one-way roads or to dead ends, and points mobile users to offline maps for areas without cell service. Sources: [Smokies directions & GPS warning](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/directions.htm)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

## All active Great Smoky Mountains NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Seasonal road closures.** Heintooga Ridge Road, Parson Branch Road, and Rich Mountain Road are closed for the season. (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **[Park Closure] Park Headquarters Road is closed.** Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.
- **[Park Closure] Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road closed..** Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road (Heintooga Round-Bottom Road) are closed. (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **[Information] Most visitors need a parking tag.** All vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes require a parking tag. Three tag durations are available for purchase for all vehicle sizes and types: Daily ($5), Weekly ($15), or Annual ($40). (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

# Great Smoky Mountains Townsend Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Great Smoky Mountains National Park · Townsend, TN (TN-73) · Status: **Open — Winter Weather Advisory**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/townsend-entrance.html

The Townsend entrance on TN-73 is the 'quiet side' gateway to Little River Road, Laurel Creek Road and Cades Cove.

## This week at the Townsend Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Little River Road and Laurel Creek Road: primary roads, open 24/7 year-round, weather permitting. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
- **Open:** Cades Cove Loop Road: open sunrise to sunset daily, weather permitting. Sources: [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **Closed:** Rich Mountain Road and Parson Branch Road (out of Cades Cove) are closed for the season. Forge Creek Road is open through Dec 31, subject to closures for snow, ice or mud. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **Heads-up:** NWS Winter Weather Advisory for the area, issued Nov 11, until 7 am EST Nov 14. Sources: [NWS Morristown: Winter Weather Advisory (issued Nov 11, until Nov 14 7 am EST)](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=35.685&lon=-83.537)
- **Info:** Parking tags are sold at The Great Smokies Welcome Center in Townsend, Cades Cove Visitor Center and the Tremont Institute store. Cades Cove Campground is open year-round. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [Smokies current conditions & trail closures](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

**Entrance fee:** No entrance fee. A parking tag is required for any vehicle parked more than 15 minutes: daily $5, weekly $15, annual $40. America the Beautiful passes are not accepted in place of a tag. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [NPS Great Smoky Mountains fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

## Forecast near the Townsend Entrance

- **NWS Winter Weather Advisory:** Winter Weather Advisory issued November 11 at 11:09PM EST until November 14 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Morristown TN

|---|---|---|---|
| Overnight | 45°F | Rain Showers Likely | 10 to 15 mph |
| Thursday | 53°F | Chance Rain Showers | 10 to 15 mph |

| Friday | 44°F | Rain And Snow Showers Likely | 5 mph |

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Bear jams in Cades Cove.** Cades Cove is one of the park's best places to see bears, and one of the easiest places to get too close. Approaching within 50 yards is illegal. Use pull-offs and don't stop in the road. Sources: [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm); [Smokies black bears](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/nature/black-bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Cold rain into freezing nights.** NWS forecast for Townsend: rain showers Thursday around 53°F, rain and snow showers likely Friday, and a low near 30°F Friday night. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Little River's slick rocks.** Wet rocks and cold water make the Little River a fall and hypothermia risk. NPS links to USGS gauges for current flow. Sources: [Smokies current conditions & trail closures](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides

## Checklist for the Townsend Entrance

- [ ] **Parking tag before Cades Cove** — Required for stops over 15 minutes.
- [ ] **Time Cades Cove for daylight** — The loop is open sunrise to sunset.
- [ ] **Download GOES in Townsend** — Before you head up Little River Road.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Great Smoky Mountains Cherokee Entrance (Oconaluftee): this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Great Smoky Mountains National Park · Cherokee, NC (US-441) · Status: **Open — elk area**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/great-smoky-mountains/cherokee-entrance.html

The Cherokee entrance on US-441 in North Carolina leads to Oconaluftee Visitor Center and the Mountain Farm Museum, then north up Newfound Gap Road to the state line.

## This week at the Cherokee Entrance (Oconaluftee) (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** Newfound Gap Road (US-441): open 24/7 year-round, weather permitting. Snow showers are forecast at Newfound Gap Friday. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
- **Closed:** Heintooga Ridge Road (off the Blue Ridge Parkway) is closed for the season, and Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road are closed. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **Open:** Kuwohi Road: open through Nov 29, subject to closures for snow and ice. Sources: [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **Info:** Cataloochee Road: a year-round gravel road that may close for snow and ice. Sources: [Smokies seasonal road schedule (2026 season)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **Info:** Parking tags are sold at Oconaluftee Visitor Center and Kuwohi Visitor Center, and online. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

**Entrance fee:** No entrance fee. A parking tag is required for any vehicle parked more than 15 minutes: daily $5, weekly $15, annual $40. America the Beautiful passes are not accepted in place of a tag. Sources: [NPS Great Smoky Mountains alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [NPS Great Smoky Mountains fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Elk in the Oconaluftee fields.** Stay at least 25 yards (75 ft) from elk; bulls in the fall rut can charge people, cars and pets.   - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals

Sources: [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals

  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

- **Black bears.** Over the last 10 years the Smokies averaged 339 reported negative human–bear encounters a year. In fall, bears feed heavily (up to 20,000 calories a day) and show up near roadsides. Approaching within 50 yards (150 ft) is illegal. If a black bear attacks and isn't after your food, fight back; don't play dead. Sources: [Smokies black bears](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/nature/black-bears.htm); [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Elk.** It's illegal to approach elk within 25 yards (75 ft). During the fall rut, bulls can be aggressive toward people, vehicles and pets. NPS closed the fields around Oconaluftee and Cataloochee to visitors during the rut, so obey any posted closures. Sources: [News release: View elk and black bears safely this fall (Sep 14, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-to-view-elk-and-black-bears-safely-this-fall.htm); [News release: Approaching elk is dangerous and illegal (Oct 7, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-reminds-visitors-approaching-elk-is-both-dangerous-and-illegal.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for dangerous animals
- **Wet cold and fast-changing mountain weather.** Temperatures can vary 10–20°F between base and summit, and clear skies lower down don't guarantee the same up high. Rain, then snow, then near-freezing nights is a textbook setup for hypothermia. Sources: [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **GPS and no signal.** NPS warns that GPS units may send drivers the wrong way on one-way roads or to dead ends, and points mobile users to offline maps for areas without cell service. Sources: [Smokies directions & GPS warning](https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/directions.htm)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

## All active Great Smoky Mountains NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Seasonal road closures.** Heintooga Ridge Road, Parson Branch Road, and Rich Mountain Road are closed for the season. (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **[Park Closure] Park Headquarters Road is closed.** Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.
- **[Park Closure] Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road closed..** Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road (Heintooga Round-Bottom Road) are closed. (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/seasonalroads.htm)
- **[Information] Most visitors need a parking tag.** All vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes require a parking tag. Three tag durations are available for purchase for all vehicle sizes and types: Daily ($5), Weekly ($15), or Annual ($40). (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

# Zion National Park this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · UT · Shuttle season ends Nov 28; cool days, cold canyon water, storms Friday night. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/

Zion is open 24/7 year-round. The Zion Canyon shuttle is on its late-fall schedule through Nov 28 (first bus 7 am, last bus up-canyon 5 pm, last bus out of Temple of Sinawava 6:15 pm), with no shuttle service Nov 29 – Dec 25. NWS forecasts sunny days Thursday, then rain and thunderstorms Friday night into Saturday. The Narrows closes whenever NWS issues a Flash Flood Warning or the Virgin River tops 150 cfs. Sources: [Zion Canyon shuttle schedule](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/zion-canyon-shuttle-system.htm); [Zion operating hours & facility hours](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

## Entrances open this week

- [South Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/south-entrance.md) (Springdale, UT (SR-9)): **Open — shuttle through Nov 28**. The South Entrance at Springdale leads to the Zion Canyon Visitor Center, where shuttles leave for the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive, the Riverside Walk and The Narrows.
- [East Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/east-entrance.md) (Mt. Carmel Junction, UT (SR-9)): **Open — gravel section, size limits**. The East Entrance west of Mt. Carmel Junction starts the Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway: slickrock country, the Canyon Overlook Trail, and the historic tunnel down to Zion Canyon.
- [Kolob Canyons Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/kolob-canyons-entrance.md) (I-15 Exit 40 (near Cedar City)): **Open — may close for snow or ice**. Kolob Canyons is Zion's quieter northwest district, at I-15 Exit 40, 17 miles south of Cedar City and about an hour from Zion Canyon. A five-mile scenic drive leads to viewpoints and wilderness trails.

## Closed or limited this week

- **Watchman Trail.** Closed pending repairs. Sources: [NPS Zion alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Hidden Canyon / Observation Point from Zion Canyon.** The East Rim Trail is partially closed by a large rockfall: Hidden Canyon is closed, and Observation Point can only be reached from the east. Sources: [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Angels Landing requires a separate permit. Sources: [NPS Zion fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [Angels Landing permits](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)

## What matters in Zion right now

- **Flash floods.** Flash floods can happen at any time in Zion, carrying trees and boulders. The Narrows closes when flow exceeds 150 cfs or when NWS issues a Flash Flood Warning. Rain and thunderstorms are forecast Friday night into Saturday this week. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm); [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts
- **Toxic cyanobacteria.** Don't drink water from rivers, streams or pools, and don't submerge your head in them. Use potable water, and treat spring water only as a last resort. Sources: [Zion toxic cyanobacteria advisory](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/toxic-cyanobacteria-bloom-in-the-virgin-river-and-the-streams-of-zion-national-park.htm); [NPS Zion alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Hypothermia in the canyons.** NPS: hypothermia is a major hazard in narrow canyons, and immersion in water is the fastest way to lose body heat. Avoid cotton and eat before you get chilled. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Cliffs.** Falls from cliffs on trails have caused deaths. Loose sand on stone is slippery, so stay on the trail and back from edges. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides

## Active Zion NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Watchman Trail closed.** The Watchman Trail is closed pending repairs.
- **[Caution] Large vehicle restrictions on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway.** Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/large-vehicles.htm)
- **[Caution] Toxic cyanobacteria in rivers, streams, and pools.** Do not submerge your head in or drink instream water in Zion National Park. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/toxic-cyanobacteria-bloom-in-the-virgin-river-and-the-streams-of-zion-national-park.htm)
- **[Information] Angels Landing Pilot Permit Program.** All hikers need a permit to hike Angels Landing. Learn why you need a permit and how to get one using the link below. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)
- **[Information] Please park legally and responsibly.** Zion has limited parking. Once parking spaces in Zion are full, visitors should park in Springdale. Please park only in designated spaces. Vehicles parked outside of designated spaces are subject to citation and towing. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/traffic.htm#parking)

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Zion South Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Zion National Park · Springdale, UT (SR-9) · Status: **Open — shuttle through Nov 28**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/south-entrance.html

The South Entrance at Springdale leads to the Zion Canyon Visitor Center, where shuttles leave for the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive, the Riverside Walk and The Narrows.

## This week at the South Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Zion Canyon shuttle, Oct 25 – Nov 28: first bus 7 am from the Visitor Center, last bus up-canyon 5 pm, last bus out of Temple of Sinawava 6:15 pm. No service Nov 29 – Dec 25. Springdale Line: 8 am – 6 pm through Nov 28. Sources: [Zion Canyon shuttle schedule](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/zion-canyon-shuttle-system.htm)
- **Info:** Zion Canyon Visitor Center, park store and wilderness desk: 8 am – 5 pm. Human History Museum: 10 am – 5 pm. Sources: [Zion operating hours & facility hours](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
- **Closed:** Watchman Trail is closed pending repairs and Hidden Canyon is closed (rockfall). Angels Landing requires a permit. Sources: [NPS Zion alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Angels Landing permits](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Parking is limited. When park lots fill, park in Springdale; vehicles outside designated spaces can be cited and towed. Sources: [NPS Zion alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Info:** Watchman Campground is open year-round (reservations required). South Campground closes seasonally in winter. Sources: [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Zion operating hours & facility hours](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/hours.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Angels Landing requires a separate permit. Sources: [NPS Zion fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [Angels Landing permits](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **The Narrows in November.** Cold water and short days. Check USGS flow and the NWS forecast the morning you go; the route closes at 150 cfs or under a Flash Flood Warning. Showers and thunderstorms are forecast Friday night and Saturday. Sources: [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Don't miss the last shuttle.** NPS says not to wait for the last shuttle of the day. Being stuck in the canyon after dark in November means a long, cold walk out. Sources: [Zion Canyon shuttle schedule](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/zion-canyon-shuttle-system.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Cyanobacteria in the Virgin River.** Don't drink river water or put your head under. NPS's advisory covers rivers, streams and pools parkwide. Sources: [Zion toxic cyanobacteria advisory](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/toxic-cyanobacteria-bloom-in-the-virgin-river-and-the-streams-of-zion-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides

## Checklist for the South Entrance

- [ ] **Arrive early or park in Springdale** — Lots fill, and towing is enforced.
- [ ] **Note the last shuttle times** — Last bus up-canyon 5 pm; last out 6:15 pm through Nov 28.
- [ ] **A gallon of water per person per day** — NPS's desert rule applies even when it's cool.
- [ ] **Download GOES in Springdale** — Don't count on coverage in the canyon.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Zion East Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Zion National Park · Mt. Carmel Junction, UT (SR-9) · Status: **Open — gravel section, size limits**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/east-entrance.html

The East Entrance west of Mt. Carmel Junction starts the Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway: slickrock country, the Canyon Overlook Trail, and the historic tunnel down to Zion Canyon.

## This week at the East Entrance (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** The Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway reopened to visitors Oct 9 after a Sept 30 rockfall. One section is temporarily gravel until it's repaved, so drive with caution and watch for crews and pedestrians. Sources: [News release: Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway reopens (Oct 9, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/learn/news/2026-10-09-zmch.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Large-vehicle restrictions: vehicles over the length, width, height or weight limits can't travel between Canyon Junction and the East Entrance and must go around through Springdale. Sources: [NPS Zion alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Zion large-vehicle restrictions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/large-vehicles.htm)
- **Open:** Personal vehicles are allowed on the Zion–Mt. Carmel Highway year-round, including during shuttle season. Sources: [Zion operating hours & facility hours](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/hours.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Angels Landing requires a separate permit. Sources: [NPS Zion fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [Angels Landing permits](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)

## Forecast near the East Entrance

| Period | Temp | Forecast | Wind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tonight | 37°F | Clear | 12 mph |
| Thursday | 61°F | Sunny | 6 to 12 mph |
| Thursday Night | 38°F | Partly Cloudy | 12 mph |
| Friday | 56°F | Partly Sunny then Chance Light Rain | 3 to 10 mph |
| Friday Night | 39°F | Light Rain then Showers And Thunderstorms | 3 to 14 mph |
| Saturday | 45°F | Showers And Thunderstorms | 5 to 15 mph |
| Saturday Night | 28°F | Mostly Clear | 5 mph |
| Sunday | 50°F | Mostly Sunny | 0 to 6 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.234&lon=-112.876

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Slickrock edges.** Canyon Overlook and the slickrock pullouts have drop-offs. Sand on stone is slippery: stay back from edges and watch kids. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Colder, higher side of the park.** NWS forecast near the East Entrance: lows in the upper 30s, highs around 56–61°F, then rain and thunderstorms Friday night into Saturday. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Lightning and flash floods.** Storms are in the forecast. NPS warns flash floods can occur at any time in Zion; avoid washes and narrow canyons when storms are around. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

## Checklist for the East Entrance

- [ ] **Check your vehicle size** — Oversize vehicles must go around through Springdale.
- [ ] **Allow time for the gravel section** — A temporary surface after the rockfall.
- [ ] **Download GOES before Mt. Carmel Junction** — Plan for thin coverage on the east side.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

## Zion park-wide

- **Flash floods.** Flash floods can happen at any time in Zion, carrying trees and boulders. The Narrows closes when flow exceeds 150 cfs or when NWS issues a Flash Flood Warning. Rain and thunderstorms are forecast Friday night into Saturday this week. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm); [Zion Current Conditions](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts
- **Toxic cyanobacteria.** Don't drink water from rivers, streams or pools, and don't submerge your head in them. Use potable water, and treat spring water only as a last resort. Sources: [Zion toxic cyanobacteria advisory](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/toxic-cyanobacteria-bloom-in-the-virgin-river-and-the-streams-of-zion-national-park.htm); [NPS Zion alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides
- **Hypothermia in the canyons.** NPS: hypothermia is a major hazard in narrow canyons, and immersion in water is the fastest way to lose body heat. Avoid cotton and eat before you get chilled. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Cliffs.** Falls from cliffs on trails have caused deaths. Loose sand on stone is slippery, so stay on the trail and back from edges. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: Offline interactive health assessment + 50+ visual how-to guides

## All active Zion NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Watchman Trail closed.** The Watchman Trail is closed pending repairs.
- **[Caution] Large vehicle restrictions on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway.** Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/large-vehicles.htm)
- **[Caution] Toxic cyanobacteria in rivers, streams, and pools.** Do not submerge your head in or drink instream water in Zion National Park. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/toxic-cyanobacteria-bloom-in-the-virgin-river-and-the-streams-of-zion-national-park.htm)
- **[Information] Angels Landing Pilot Permit Program.** All hikers need a permit to hike Angels Landing. Learn why you need a permit and how to get one using the link below. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)
- **[Information] Please park legally and responsibly.** Zion has limited parking. Once parking spaces in Zion are full, visitors should park in Springdale. Please park only in designated spaces. Vehicles parked outside of designated spaces are subject to citation and towing. (https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/traffic.htm#parking)

# Zion Kolob Canyons Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Zion National Park · I-15 Exit 40 (near Cedar City) · Status: **Open — may close for snow or ice**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/zion/kolob-canyons-entrance.html

Kolob Canyons is Zion's quieter northwest district, at I-15 Exit 40, 17 miles south of Cedar City and about an hour from Zion Canyon. A five-mile scenic drive leads to viewpoints and wilderness trails.

## This week at the Kolob Canyons Entrance (official conditions)

- **Info:** Kolob Canyons Visitor Center: 8 am – 12 pm and 1 pm – 5 pm. All visitors must stop to show a pass or pay the entrance fee. The Kolob wilderness desk is closed until further notice; get wilderness permits in Zion Canyon. Sources: [Zion operating hours & facility hours](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [Kolob Canyons](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/kolob-canyons.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Kolob Canyons Road may close in winter for snow or ice, and pedestrians may not walk the road during plowing. Sources: [Kolob Canyons](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/kolob-canyons.htm)
- **Open:** Personal vehicles are allowed on Kolob Canyons Scenic Drive year-round. Sources: [Zion operating hours & facility hours](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/hours.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35. Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Angels Landing requires a separate permit. Sources: [NPS Zion fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm); [Angels Landing permits](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/angels-landing-hiking-permits.htm)

|---|---|---|---|
| Tonight | 39°F | Clear | 7 mph |
| Thursday | 61°F | Sunny | 5 to 9 mph |
| Thursday Night | 41°F | Partly Cloudy | 5 to 8 mph |
| Friday | 56°F | Mostly Sunny then Chance Light Rain | 8 to 14 mph |
| Friday Night | 40°F | Light Rain then Showers And Thunderstorms | 8 to 17 mph |
| Saturday | 46°F | Showers And Thunderstorms | 2 to 17 mph |
| Saturday Night | 31°F | Areas Of Frost | 5 mph |
| Sunday | 50°F | Areas Of Frost then Mostly Sunny | 1 to 5 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=37.453&lon=-113.225

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Cold, exposed wilderness trails.** NWS forecast for Kolob: highs near 56–61°F, lows around 40°F, and showers and thunderstorms Friday night into Saturday. These are designated wilderness trails with few people around to help. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [Kolob Canyons](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/kolob-canyons.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Flash floods in narrow canyons.** Know the forecast before entering any narrow canyon and have a plan to reach high ground. Sources: [Zion safety: flash floods, cliffs, hypothermia, water](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/safety.htm)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

# Glacier National Park this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · MT · Going-to-the-Sun Road closed at Avalanche Creek and Jackson Glacier Overlook for the season. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/

Glacier is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, but it's in its late-fall, low-service season. Going-to-the-Sun Road is closed for the season at Avalanche Creek on the west side and at Jackson Glacier Overlook on the east. The lower road from West Glacier to Lake McDonald Lodge is plowed year-round, weather permitting. There's no fuel inside the park and no in-park lodging this time of year. Entrance fees still apply; use the self-pay stations when entrances aren't staffed. Sources: [NPS Glacier alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Glacier: visiting in winter](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/winter.htm); [Glacier directions, transportation & road status](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/directions.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## Entrances open this week

- [West Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/west-entrance.md) (West Glacier, MT (US-2)): **Open — road to Avalanche Creek**. The West Entrance at West Glacier is the park's year-round front door to Apgar Village, Lake McDonald and the lower Going-to-the-Sun Road. It's about 33 miles from Kalispell.
- [St. Mary Entrance](https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/st-mary-entrance.md) (St. Mary, MT (US-89)): **Open — road to Jackson Glacier Overlook**. St. Mary is the east-side entrance to Going-to-the-Sun Road, along St. Mary Lake. It's about 125 miles from Great Falls via US-89 and Browning.

## Closed or limited this week

- **Going-to-the-Sun Road alpine section (Logan Pass).** Closed for the season between Avalanche Creek (west) and Jackson Glacier Overlook (east). Open sections may change at any time due to winter weather. Sources: [NPS Glacier alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Many Glacier and Two Medicine.** No entrance pages this week. NPS says Many Glacier Road closes the third weekend in November (weather permitting) and Two Medicine Road closes once snow requires it. Confirm on the NPS road status map, or text GNPROADS to 333111. Sources: [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [Glacier directions, transportation & road status](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/directions.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (self-pay when stations are unstaffed). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Glacier fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

## What matters in Glacier right now

- **Grizzly and black bears.** Glacier has habitat for nearly 1,000 bears of both species. Stay 100 yards from bears and wolves (25 yards from other wildlife), carry bear spray, make noise and hike in groups: Glacier has had no reported attacks on groups of four or more. In fall, bears forage hard before denning. Sources: [Glacier bear safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/bears.htm); [Glacier current conditions & safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Cold water.** Water is the number one cause of fatalities in Glacier. Use extreme caution near lakes and streams. Sources: [Glacier current conditions & safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Tularemia.** NPS confirmed tularemia in dead snowshoe hares in Many Glacier (Oct 15 release) and the St. Mary Lake area (Sept 17 release). Use insect repellent, check for ticks, don't touch carcasses, drink only treated or boiled water, and see a doctor if you get fever, chills or sores within two weeks of your visit. Sources: [News release: Tularemia detected in Many Glacier Valley (Oct 15, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/learn/news/tularemia-detected-in-glacier-national-park-s-many-glacier-valley.htm); [News release: Tularemia detected in St. Mary Lake area (Sep 17, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/learn/news/tularemia-detected-in-st-mary-lake-area-of-glacier-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Tick Risk: location- and season-specific tick activity
- **Winter self-sufficiency.** Most businesses and services in and near the park are closed from early October to late May. Expect cold, blustery days and be entirely self-sufficient. Sources: [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [Glacier current conditions & safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments

## Active Glacier NPS alerts

From the NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live: https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

- **[Park Closure] Going-to-the-Sun Road Seasonal Closure.** Going-to-the-Sun Road is closed for the season at Avalanche Creek on the west side of the park. On the east side, the closure is located at Jackson Glacier Overlook. Travel on open sections of the road may change at any time due to winter weather conditions. Visitors should check road conditions before their arrival and be prepared for winter weather. (https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/directions.htm)

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Glacier West Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Glacier National Park · West Glacier, MT (US-2) · Status: **Open — road to Avalanche Creek**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/west-entrance.html

The West Entrance at West Glacier is the park's year-round front door to Apgar Village, Lake McDonald and the lower Going-to-the-Sun Road. It's about 33 miles from Kalispell.

## This week at the West Entrance (official conditions)

- **Open:** Going-to-the-Sun Road is open from West Glacier and closed for the season at Avalanche Creek. NPS's winter page says the road from West Glacier to Lake McDonald Lodge is plowed year-round, weather permitting. Sources: [NPS Glacier alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [Glacier: visiting in winter](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/winter.htm)
- **Info:** Beyond the closure gate, the unplowed road is open to hikers and bicyclists, and to skiing and snowshoeing once there's snow. Sources: [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [Glacier: visiting in winter](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/winter.htm)
- **Info:** Apgar Visitor Center restrooms are open year-round, with a water bottle filling station (about 2 miles north of the entrance). NPS's winter page says the visitor center opens on weekends in winter. Sources: [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm); [Glacier: visiting in winter](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/winter.htm)
- **Info:** Apgar Campground offers primitive camping (vault toilet, no running water, first-come, first-served). There's no lodging in the park this time of year. Sources: [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
- **Info:** No fuel inside the park. Road alerts: text GNPROADS to 333111, tune to Travelers' Information Station 1610 AM, or call 406-888-7800. Sources: [Glacier directions, transportation & road status](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/directions.htm); [Glacier: visiting in winter](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/winter.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (self-pay when stations are unstaffed). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Glacier fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

| Sunday | 48°F | Partly Sunny | 3 mph |

Snapshot from the National Weather Service, fetched Nov 12, 2026. Live forecast: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=48.502&lon=-113.987

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **Bears on the lower road and trails.** Bears may still be active and foraging before denning. Carry bear spray, call out and clap (NPS says bells aren't enough), and don't stop near roadside bears: drive at least 100 yards past before pulling over. Sources: [Glacier bear safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/bears.htm); [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Lake McDonald's cold water.** Water is the park's top cause of death. Slick shoreline rocks and near-freezing water make a fall dangerous within minutes. Sources: [Glacier current conditions & safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Fog and short days.** NWS forecast for West Glacier this week: areas of fog, highs near 50–54°F, lows near 35°F, and a slight chance of light rain Saturday. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/)
  - In GOES: 125+ extreme weather alerts

## Checklist for the West Entrance

- [ ] **Fuel and food in West Glacier or Columbia Falls** — No gas in the park; Apgar's camp store may or may not be open.
- [ ] **Bear spray, even for short walks** — NPS: bears may still be active.
- [ ] **Pay at the self-pay station** — Fees apply when the booth is unstaffed.
- [ ] **Download GOES before the entrance** — Plan for no signal past Apgar.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.

# Glacier St. Mary Entrance: this week

> Week of Nov 9–15, 2026 · Glacier National Park · St. Mary, MT (US-89) · Status: **Open — road to Jackson Glacier Overlook**. Facts fetched Nov 12, 2026 from official NPS and NWS sources.

HTML version: https://parks.goes.health/parks/glacier/st-mary-entrance.html

St. Mary is the east-side entrance to Going-to-the-Sun Road, along St. Mary Lake. It's about 125 miles from Great Falls via US-89 and Browning.

## This week at the St. Mary Entrance (official conditions)

- **Heads-up:** Going-to-the-Sun Road is closed for the season at Jackson Glacier Overlook on the east side. Open sections can change at any time due to winter weather. Sources: [NPS Glacier alerts (NPS Data API, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm)
- **Closed:** St. Mary Visitor Center is closed for the winter. Primitive camping is available year-round at St. Mary Campground. Sources: [Glacier: visiting in winter](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/winter.htm); [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm)
- **Heads-up:** Tularemia was confirmed in a dead snowshoe hare in the St. Mary Lake area (Sept 17 release). Sources: [News release: Tularemia detected in St. Mary Lake area (Sep 17, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/learn/news/tularemia-detected-in-st-mary-lake-area-of-glacier-national-park.htm)
- **Info:** No fuel inside the park. The St. Mary grocery store sometimes stays open in fall; full-service groceries are in Browning. Sources: [Glacier directions, transportation & road status](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/directions.htm); [Glacier operating hours & seasons](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/hours.htm)

**Entrance fee:** Private vehicle $35 (self-pay when stations are unstaffed). Non-US residents 16+ pay an additional $100 nonresident fee unless entering with an annual / America the Beautiful pass. Sources: [NPS Glacier fees & passes](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/fees.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)

| Friday Night | 36°F | Partly Cloudy | 3 mph |

## What actually matters here this season

The goal is a good trip, not a scary one. These are the hazards NPS highlights for this area and season, and what to do about each.

- **East-side wind and cold.** Glacier sits where Pacific air from the west meets arctic air from the northeast. NWS forecast for St. Mary this week: mostly cloudy, highs around 54–62°F, lows near 36–46°F. Expect colder, harsher conditions higher up. Sources: [National Weather Service point forecasts (api.weather.gov, fetched Nov 12)](https://www.weather.gov/); [Glacier current conditions & safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/conditions.htm); [NPS Data API (parks, operating hours, fees)](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/developer/api-documentation.htm)
  - In GOES: Environmental Health: hypothermia and frostbite assessments
- **Bears.** Grizzlies and black bears live on both sides of the Divide. Make noise, hike in a group, and carry bear spray where you can reach it. Sources: [Glacier bear safety](https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/bears.htm)
  - In GOES: Wildlife Encounters: location-specific risk indicators for bears and other dangerous animals
- **Tularemia and ticks.** Don't touch dead animals, use repellent, check for ticks, and drink only treated or boiled water. Sources: [News release: Tularemia detected in St. Mary Lake area (Sep 17, 2026)](https://www.nps.gov/glac/learn/news/tularemia-detected-in-st-mary-lake-area-of-glacier-national-park.htm)
  - In GOES: Tick Risk: location- and season-specific tick activity

## Checklist for the St. Mary Entrance

- [ ] **Fuel and supplies in Browning or St. Mary** — No fuel in the park.
- [ ] **Bear spray and windproof layers** — The east side is exposed.
- [ ] **Treat all water** — Tularemia advisory in the St. Mary Lake area.
- [ ] **Download GOES before St. Mary** — Plan for no signal inside the park.

Follow official NPS rules, posted closures and ranger instructions. They override anything on this page.
